prompt: A surveyor stands $15$ m from the base of a tower and sights the top, which is $40$ m above eye level. What is the angle of elevation, in degrees, rounded to one decimal place?
hint: The $40$ m is opposite the angle of elevation and the $15$ m is adjacent to it.

hints.text: The $40$ m is opposite the angle of elevation and the $15$ m is adjacent to it.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $10$ m across and $10$ m up: $\tan\theta = \frac{10}{10} = 1$, so $\theta = 45^\circ$. The opposite side goes on top every time, and here that is the $40$.

explanation: Sketch the right triangle: the horizontal leg is $15$ m and the vertical leg is $40$ m.
The angle of elevation sits at the surveyor, so the $40$ is opposite and the $15$ is adjacent: $\tan\theta = \frac{40}{15} \approx 2.667$.
Undo the tangent: $\theta = \arctan(2.667) \approx 69.44^\circ$, which rounds to $69.4^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check it against $45^\circ$
steps: If the tower were $15$ m tall, the rise would equal the run and the angle would be exactly $45^\circ$.
The tower is much taller than that, so the sightline is much steeper than $45^\circ$.
$69.4^\circ$ is comfortably steeper — the answer is in the right neighbourhood.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The classic wrong answer is $20.6^\circ$, from computing $\arctan\left(\frac{15}{40}\right)$ with the ratio upside down.
Notice that $20.6^\circ$ and $69.4^\circ$ add to $90^\circ$ — flipping the ratio hands you the OTHER angle in the triangle, the one at the top of the tower.
Fix it by labelling the sketch before you touch the calculator: mark which leg is opposite the angle you actually want, and put that one on top.
